solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Short major in hunky chap

indicators.note: a word that is cut short loses its final letter

blocks.note: in American usage to major in a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: An army major cuts a fine figure inside a muscular man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like a military rank, but 'major in' is the American college verb meaning to study; STUDY cut short is STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexually attractive, muscular young man.

clue.text: Curvy figure about right, a bit of a looker

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a cone is a solid with a curved surface
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shapely woman is described as rather good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a looker' sounds like praise for someone attractive, but read literally it means a part of something that looks: an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye, a part of the organ we look with.

clue.text: Out to eat game – last day of Lent perhaps?

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to go forth is to go out
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Someone heads out to a game for dinner on the eve of Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a British name for a knockout match. Lent traditionally lasts forty days, hence the question mark and 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent counts forty days of fasting, so its final day would be numbered the fortieth.

clue.text: Brothers: those cooking for the audience?

indicators.note: something done for an audience is heard rather than read, so we go by sound

blocks.note: people who cook in a pan are fryers

explanation.surface: A group of brothers puts on a cookery show in front of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: Brothers here are members of a religious order, not siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Friars are male members of mendicant religious orders and are addressed as Brother.

clue.text: General character digitally reduced?

blocks.note: surface reading: a broad, overall quality or nature
setter's reading: a General whose size is cut down to that of a finger

explanation.surface: A general quality has been shrunk by computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is a title, not an adjective: the tiny showman Charles Stratton performed as General Tom Thumb, named after the folk hero no bigger than a thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale figure was as small as a digit, and the circus performer used a military title.

clue.text: Insignificant storm brewing in this?

blocks.note: surface reading: a minor tempest gathering
setter's reading: the idiom about a fuss over nothing names a vessel where tea brews

explanation.surface: A small squall is gathering somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a storm in a teacup' means a big fuss about something trivial; 'brewing' doubles as what tea does.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom places a trivial commotion inside this small china vessel used for drinking hot drinks.

clue.text: Eye infection covered by ophthalmologist yesterday

indicators.note: what is covered is concealed beneath other words, so look inside them

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An eye doctor dealt with an infected eye yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles ophthalmologi-ST YE-sterday; the eye-doctor setting makes it easy to hunt for the condition rather than the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid caused by a bacterial infection of a gland.

clue.text: Irish flag perhaps in court, or I waved around Lithuania’s first

indicators.note: something waved is shaken about, so these letters are jumbled
to go around something is to enclose it
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: In court, someone waves an Irish flag in support of Lithuania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In court' looks like part of the scene, but 'in' joins definition to wordplay and 'court' is anagram fodder; waved also suits a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish national flag has three vertical bands of green, white and orange, making it a three-coloured flag.

clue.text: Youth I think filled with ambition at last

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside
at last points to the final letter of a word

blocks.note: to fancy is to think or suppose
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young person feels full of ambition at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' is a British way of saying 'I think' or 'I suppose', and the single letter sits just after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth as the early stage of life covers infancy, the earliest period of childhood.

clue.text: Open on time

blocks.note: on top of is over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A shop opens punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open on time' reads like a promise about trading hours; 'Open' is an adjective meaning not hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done publicly and without concealment, the adjective sense of not hidden.

clue.text: The certified tale in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A story vouched for as genuine appears in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like the start of the sentence, yet it is the whole definition; 'novel' is the anagram signal, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the word 'the' is classed as the definite article, contrasting with indefinite 'a' and 'an'.

clue.text: Group needing time for dressing

indicators.note: one thing needing another wants it attached alongside

blocks.note: a band is a group, as of musicians
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A band needs time to get changed before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests putting on clothes; here it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound dressing is a strip of material applied to protect an injury, which is what a bandage is.

clue.text: Chancellor’s plan not entirely bringing shift

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so a letter is dropped from the end

blocks.note: the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, sets out an annual budget

explanation.surface: The finance minister's half-finished plan brings a change of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister, who presents the yearly budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move or shift position slightly, usually used of something stubborn.

clue.text: Completely lost? That’s one way to get out

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a dismissal; the answer is the past participle used of a batsman

blocks.note: first meaning: utterly baffled
second meaning: a cricket dismissal where the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of his ground

explanation.surface: Someone hopelessly lost wonders how to find an exit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman can be 'out' in several ways; being stumped by the wicketkeeper is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being baffled is an idiomatic sense, and a batsman given out this way is described with the same word.

clue.text: Ultimately drenched or soggy, the paper towel for example?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take each word's final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A paper towel ends up drenched and soggy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes with a question mark because a towel is an example of something that dries, not the usual appliance meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel removes moisture from skin, so it is literally a thing that dries, playfully called a dryer.

clue.text: Far too expensive – or is it a steal?

definitions.note: a noun phrase where the answer is a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a blatant overcharge
second meaning: a theft, here one carried out openly in broad day

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a price is outrageous or a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A steal' usually means a bargain, the opposite of overpriced; here it means a literal theft.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes outrageous overcharging, and taken literally it names a theft committed in broad day.

clue.text: Source of information, testament featuring in entire broadcast

indicators.note: something featuring in another appears within it
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
NT is the abbreviation for New Testament

explanation.surface: A source of information is a will read out in full on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suits the source-of-information theme, but it is the anagram signal for the six-letter word; the abbreviation sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide computer network is where most people now look things up, so it serves as an information source.

clue.text: Stone thrown initially into rising river, went very quickly

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the opening letter
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the letters run backwards
something put into another goes inside it

blocks.note: a rock is a stone
the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stone thrown into a river moved fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a stock crossword river; read upwards it splits around the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rocket is to move or rise with great speed, like a rocket being launched.

clue.text: Call to fighters when grenade goes off

indicators.note: something that goes off explodes, scattering its parts into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers hear a warning shout as a grenade explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: The battlefield picture suggests soldiers, but the fighters are fencers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencers are warned to take up a guard position with this French phrase before a bout begins.

clue.text: Precisely ten perform in Cambridgeshire city

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
X is the Roman numeral for ten
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Exactly ten people put on a show in an English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire in eastern England, and it opens around the two joined pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning accurately or in every detail, interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Shady alcove found in port, top taken off

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

blocks.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A shady nook is discovered in a port whose roof has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' is the link, not a hidden-word signal: the answer is not inside 'port' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a leafy garden bower, a sheltered recess shaded by climbing plants or trees.

clue.text: A shade spineless?

blocks.note: first meaning: a colour
second meaning: cowardly

explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade spineless' reads as 'a bit cowardly'; split it and 'A shade' is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a primary colour and is also slang for lacking courage, as in having a yellow streak.

clue.text: Bell failing

blocks.note: first meaning: something that clangs
second meaning: a blunder

explanation.walkthrough: To drop a clanger is a British idiom for making an embarrassing mistake; a bell is literally something that clangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing bell makes a clang, and the British idiom names a conspicuous blunder or fault.

clue.text: Trigger a devious plan to trap leader of opposition

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a ruse is a cunning trick
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sneaky scheme is set off to catch the opposition leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The political picture suggests a plot against a party leader, but only the first letter is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse a feeling or response is to provoke or set it off, a synonym of trigger as a verb.

clue.text: Poor calibre model and scoundrel – politician!

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A second-rate role model and a rogue: a typical politician!
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British centrist party; 'and' here joins two wordplay pieces rather than linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the UK Liberal Democrat party is a politician, so the definition is a general category.

clue.text: Socialist newspaper for French investors, might you say?

blocks.note: le is French for the
the FT, or Financial Times, is the British paper read by investors

explanation.surface: A left-wing paper is offered to French financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A French investor might call the Financial Times 'le FT'; that phrase run together gives the political word.
explanation.definitionFit: The political left covers socialists, so the adjective serves as a synonym for left-wing in politics.

clue.text: Kind to write

blocks.note: first meaning: a sort or category
second meaning: to produce text on a keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective for gentle, but it is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a category or sort, and as a verb it means keyboard writing.

clue.text: Loud instrument for orchestra member

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A noisy instrument is wanted for a member of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestra member' suggests a player, but it is one of the instruments in the band.
explanation.definitionFit: The flute is a woodwind instrument with a regular place in a symphony orchestra's line-up.

clue.text: Failing to start, developers lazily don’t respond to alarm call?

indicators.note: failing to start means missing the beginning, so the first letter goes
done lazily means done sloppily, so the letters end up out of order

blocks.note: the word without its opening letter

explanation.surface: Idle software developers miss the start of the day by ignoring the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to start' sounds like part of the lazy developers' story but strips a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the time you meant to wake is to ignore the alarm clock's ringing.
